decisions.reason: The bowl-removal clearance is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The same-message MODIFY already records the whisk-height, higher-RPM splash, and operating-cleanliness constraints.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already captures fast, preferably tool-free whisk removal for cleaning and event part swapping.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already records that whisk height must be optimized to produce good foam.
The source establishes layout constraints but does not select or replace any BOM component; possible guards or geometry changes remain optional design approaches.
Bowl clearance and whisk-height layout constraints do not necessarily change the electrical wiring plan.
The client mentions bowl geometry only as a possible splash-control method and does not require a specific change to bowl size, depth, or geometry.
The source does not change prolonged-use expectations or the maximum-speed duty constraint.
Higher RPM is contextual to the layout and splash constraints; the approved speed range and operating modes remain unchanged.
The source concerns mixing-area splash control and removable assemblies, not the dispensing mechanism, sequence, or flow behavior.
Keeping the machine clean from mixing splashes does not modify the existing plumbing seal or leak-prevention requirements.
The source adds mechanical layout and splash-control constraints but does not alter the requirement to isolate electrical components from liquid leakage.
